requirement: The recorded requirement text in each evidence representation MUST match all Markdown inside its fenced `{req}` directive, excluding leading and trailing whitespace and the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Habeas MUST report changed requirement text.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover both obligations of `requirements.ci.requirement_text`. They cover the match obligation and the change-reporting obligation, in both evidence representations.

**Recorded text matches all Markdown in the fenced `{req}` body, ignoring leading and trailing whitespace.**
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines]` has a body with leading blank lines and indentation. It also has a multi-line body containing a nested code fence that itself contains `{req}`. The evidence records the trimmed full text, and the test asserts that validation reports no errors.
- That test would fail if the matcher truncated at the inner fence or compared untrimmed text.

**Header option lines are excluded.**
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable]` declares a `{req}` and an `{example}` with `:test:` option lines. Their evidence records only the body text. The test asserts `!errors.contains("text changed")`, so the option lines are not counted as text.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text]` checks that `without_options` strips only the option lines directly after the opening fence. It keeps nested directive text and inline `:impl:` or `:test:` text in the body.

**Changed requirement text is reported.**
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[collects_missing_orphan_format_false_and_changed_line_errors]` records "Old text." against the declared "First.". It asserts the "requirement text changed" message and the `- Old text.` and `+ First.` diff lines.
- `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once]` covers every review kind, in both the legacy format and the native format. It first asserts there are no findings for unmodified evidence. It then mutates the `requirement` or `example` field to "Changed subject text." and asserts a "text changed" finding. It also asserts that the native findings equal the legacy findings. This covers "each evidence representation".

I found no gap. The tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, and their assertions check the required outcomes.

text: :::{req} requirement_text

The recorded requirement text in each evidence representation MUST match all Markdown inside its fenced `{req}` directive, excluding leading and trailing whitespace and the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Habeas MUST report changed requirement text.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
